policies.title: Guyana: Foreign Ministry and ISS aligned ordinary passports visa-free
policies.summary: The Foreign Ministry and Immigration Support Services schedules both directly name these nationalities without a special-passport or third-country-document condition. This is a visa exemption, not a CARICOM application, landing permit, eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: Only nationalities expressly named for ordinary passports or without a passport-type restriction in both schedules are included.

The Foreign Ministry describes CARICOM movement in its schedule, but this policy relies on the same page’s express heading that the named nationals do not require visas; it does not convert treaty movement language, CSME rights, a landing permit or a border form into a visa status.
The two current schedules state different durations for some shared nationalities, including the Dominican Republic and Panama. The classification is visa-free, but no uniform duration is assigned.

Cuba, Indonesia, Spain and Uruguay are not included because the Foreign Ministry limits their exemption to specified diplomatic, official, service or special passports while the ISS schedule presents an unqualified ordinary-passport entry.

policies.title: Guyana: Foreign Ministry named ordinary passports visa-free
policies.summary: The current Foreign Ministry schedule directly names these nationalities without a special-passport or third-country-document condition. The ISS schedule does not name them, which is not treated as a contrary rule.
conditions: Only the Foreign Ministry's explicit ordinary-passport or unqualified entries are classified. ISS omission is not converted into a visa requirement or a conflicting status.
The classification does not convert CARICOM movement language, an application form, or a third-country-document condition into a visa exemption.

policies.title: Guyana: ISS and consular Schedule 1 named ordinary passports visa-free
policies.summary: The ISS schedule and the official consular Schedule 1 directly name Lesotho and Malaysia without a special-passport or third-country-document condition. The Foreign Ministry schedule does not name them, which is not treated as a contrary rule.
conditions: Only the two explicit unqualified entries are classified; Foreign Ministry omission is not converted into a visa requirement or a conflicting status.
The ISS schedule gives Lesotho 14 days and Malaysia 60 days; no broader duration, passport type or purpose is inferred.

policies.title: Guyana: Bolivian ordinary passport tourist visa on arrival
policies.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs ISS schedule expressly identifies a tourist visa on arrival for Bolivian regular-passport holders. This is visa_on_arrival, not a visa-free or electronic route.
conditions: The stated route is limited to tourist entry with a regular passport. It does not establish a work, residence, study, transit, diplomatic, official, service or special-document route.

The Foreign Ministry separately identifies a no-visa exemption only for Bolivian diplomatic, service and official passport holders; that passport-type distinction does not contradict the ISS ordinary-passport arrival-visa route.
No fee, duration, ports, entry count, extension or pre-travel approval condition is assigned because this schedule does not state it.

conflicts.explanation: The Foreign Ministry’s current schedule expressly states that Qatari nationals do not require a visa for a period not exceeding 30 days.

unresolved.reason: The current Foreign Ministry and ISS schedules name Colombian nationals for a 90-day visa exemption, but the official consular Schedule 1 limits Colombia to diplomatic/service passports. The conflicting official ordinary-passport scope is not resolved here.

The consular advisory addresses Guyanese citizens travelling on foreign passports and requires place-of-birth or other Guyanese-origin evidence. It does not directly establish the ordinary Guyanese-passport citizenship pair, so citizenship is not inferred.

The Foreign Ministry limits Spain's exemption to diplomatic passports, while ISS and the consular Schedule 1 list Spain without that restriction. The conflicting ordinary-passport scope is not resolved here.
